expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides types.ts, useBulkSelection.ts, api/documents.ts, BulkActionsBar.tsx, DocumentsTable.tsx with all pieces present

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: Full React/TypeScript implementation with hooks, state management, and complete components

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Delete is not recoverable: 'I didn't make delete reversible (soft-delete + trash) even though that's the stronger Control-rung device... because that's a backend/schema decision outside a UI component.' Archive is reversible via undo, but Delete relies on type-to-confirm dialog alone.

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: {selectedCount.toLocaleString()} selected in bar and count shown in delete dialog: 'Delete {count.toLocaleString()} document{count === 1 ? "" : "s"}?'

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Discriminated union Selection type with kind: 'explicit' vs 'allMatching'; showSelectAllBanner only appears when 'allOnPageSelected && totalCount > pageIds.length'

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive and Delete buttons separated with distinct styling: Archive has gray border/text, Delete has red border/text. Comment: 'Destructive action: separated spatially and styled distinctly from Archive'

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Delete button is styled as secondary (border button with red text), not primary or focused

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement that server must enforce authorization, validation, or rules enforcement. Mentions idempotency keys but not server-side enforcement responsibility.

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Closing note lists Control-rung devices (double-submit guard via disabled state, discriminated union preventing ambiguous state, explicit select-all split) and items 'Left possible on purpose'
